name: Scott Adams
role: American cartoonist (Dilbert creator) and political commentator (1957-2026)
summary: Adams, creator of the Dilbert comic strip, became a political commentator through his blog and daily show Real Coffee, mostly analysing persuasion and Donald Trump. He described himself as socially liberal and result-driven, and he said he favored whatever policy works. His stated positions included pro-nuclear energy, legal marijuana and gay marriage, gun rights, school choice, opposition to affirmative action and DEI, and opposition to higher taxes on himself.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In 2019 he sketched a system in which government pays for children, seniors and lower-income adults while everyone else keeps private insurance, and said countries with universal care did not become dictatorships. He did not call for state-provided care for everyone and said he was not supporting socialism, so the record points both ways.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He called himself solidly a capitalist and said capitalism produced the wealth that other systems depend on, while also supporting some government roles such as a means-tested public health tier.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He said he does not want his own taxes to go up and that he would leave the country if his taxes reached 70%, arguing that taxing the rich would undercut the system that creates wealth.

unions-good.rationale: His remarks concern teachers unions, which he criticized; he gave no general position on labor unions.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He said he would legalize more drugs than Bernie Sanders's marijuana position, naming psychedelic mushrooms and a test on opioids, and said he favored decriminalizing marijuana. He did not call for all recreational drugs to be legal, and he proposed tough measures against fentanyl.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Reacting to a poll showing support for federal action against online hate speech, he warned about whoever decides what counts as hate speech and said 'maybe you just need free speech.'

limit-guns.rationale: He described himself as 100% pro-Second Amendment and accepting of roughly 20,000 gun deaths a year, while saying he would try some restrictions (he floated a temporary ban on gun sales to young white men) to see whether deaths fall. This leans against strict limits but is not an absolute position.

empower-police-military.rationale: A cartel strike unit and police technology are nearby; no stated position on more funding and authority for police and military.

decide-locally.rationale: He argued that states work as policy laboratories, so questions such as abortion law or marijuana can be left to states and measured by results rather than argued on principle.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In a 2020 interview he said he is socially 'lefter than the left' and asked of gay marriage 'why didn't we do that a long time ago.'

abortion-legal.rationale: He said he recuses himself from the abortion question because men should not influence it and would support whatever consensus women reach, which is not a position on legality.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: His record is mixed. In 2021 he floated a corporate-funded training scheme as a form of reparations and in a Twitter Spaces talk said cash reparations must be weighed against other uses of money; by 2023 he said race-based policies had helped but should now end, criticized DEI, ESG and critical race theory, and said it made no sense for white people to try to help Black Americans. The latest position leans against active correction.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He backed border barriers and described Trump's immigration moves, but gave no clear position of his own on immigration levels.

open-borders.rationale: He supported border barriers where needed and said free health care and unlimited immigration cannot coexist, while also floating unlimited immigration into special tracked zones. Mixed, leaning against open borders.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He said he could not judge the climate science himself and did not state a view on drastic government action.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He repeatedly called Generation IV nuclear power the obvious practical solution, said the press was failing the country by ignoring it, and said the US needs a robust nuclear industry for domestic, military and space uses.

basic-income.rationale: He called a basic income not nearly as crazy as it sounds, said as robots replace jobs it should be tested, and in 2020 said he was okay with it during the pandemic emergency. He said he was not recommending it, and preferred that people who can work do so.

political-violence-never.rationale: In January 2021 he said he opposes all forms of violence or destruction of property, while saying he would not make much of a few broken windows during a major demonstration.

military-superiority.rationale: He called national defense the country's most important priority and argued the US must lead in nuclear power for military and space use, saying whoever controls space will control the earth.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He said that on money and politics he favors whatever works and does not care where a plan comes from if someone can argue convincingly that it works.

harm-principle.rationale: He said he votes for freedom wherever people are not hurting anyone, naming marijuana and wearing dresses, and objecting to people being locked up for harmless acts. He did not state the principle as a general rule on every restriction.

school-vouchers.rationale: He criticized teachers unions for demanding bans on charter schools and private school choice and said, 'I'm in favor of school choice.' Vouchers are not named specifically.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: In 2020 he said he saw no better reason to run up the national debt than the pandemic emergency and supported paying people directly.

force-without-un.rationale: A plan to strike cartels that does not mention the UN is not a stated position on UN approval.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Linking free health care to immigration levels is nearby; no stated position on restricting benefits to citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He said he does not want to reward people for not working and wants those willing to work to hold the available jobs, but also saw a case for paying a basic income without a work requirement, so the evidence points both ways.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He said that from a constitutional and legal standpoint no one should be discriminated against for race, religion or ethnicity, and that he does not oppose the Constitution on this. His 2023 'get away' remark was described by him as hyperbole about personal choice, not law.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He said no one should be discriminated against by race, religion or ethnicity in law and no discrimination against individuals. He did not speak to moral worth in general terms.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: In February 2023 he said he had tentatively favored affirmative action but no longer did, because the gap had closed enough that ending favoritism was the best step; he repeated that race-based policies should now stop.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: He said he opposes discrimination against individuals 'in any regard, not personally, not professionally, no exceptions,' and that no one should be discriminated against by race or religion.

corporate-influence.rationale: He said it is bad enough that big corporations have influence through donations and lobbyists and that boycotts to change laws take it further, though he also said society largely accepts ordinary lobbying.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He said capitalism produced the wealth that redistribution schemes depend on and that socialism could not exist until capitalism had made people rich.

holocaust-denial.rationale: In a 2006 blog post he asked how the 6 million figure was calculated and whether it was a documented number or a round one, but wrote that 'No reasonable person doubts that the Holocaust happened.' He questioned the exact figure and did not deny the event.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: from his statement that same-sex marriage should have been legalized long ago and that he is socially left of the left.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Opposing a ban on transition is nearby; no stated position on legal recognition by gender identity.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: He said he takes ideas from either side on money and politics (socially liberal, but favoring whatever works), though he also described his own left or libertarian labels as deliberately empty.

racial-franchise.rationale: Inferred: from his statement that the law should not discriminate by race, religion or ethnicity.

notes:
He called his 'left of Bernie' and 'libertarian without the crazy parts' labels deliberately empty and said he neither voted nor joined a party, so no answer is inferred from them. Many of his statements were framed as persuasion analysis rather than his own policy view and were left null. His 2023 remarks about Black Americans were later described by him as hyperbole; the answers use what he said on policy.

Merged with an independent claude-haiku-5-5 audit: 0 answers taken from it, 2 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-haiku-5-5 notes: Living status: the Wikipedia article gives a death date of January 13, 2026, so living is false; the no-inference rule was applied anyway. Two answers have a recorded position. Persuasion analysis of Trump in Win Bigly (2017) and the podcast is not treated as his position. The 2018 'left of Bernie' and 'progressive side' self-descriptions are not mapped to any statement, because no specific policy was stated. The 2019 border-wall proposal and the 2009 post on immigration as 'as inviting as possible' were not read in full, so immigration is null. blog.dilbert.com could not be reached (DNS error), so most of his blog was read only through Goodreads mirrors and secondary reports. The 2023 remarks about Black Americans were not checked against any statement and are not counted. Win Bigly full text and Real Coffee transcripts were not obtained.
